title: Non-blocking finding from PR #418's review (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups)
description: pr-reviewer accepted PR #418 (the root-absolute-specifier fix plus extraction of the e2e-import-guard/no-restricted-src-import rule into frontend/eslint-rules/no-restricted-src-import.js with a persisted vitest test). While independently re-verifying the PR, pr-reviewer found that one of the decision entry's two stated empirical justifications for keeping the extracted module as plain JS (rather than real TypeScript) does not hold on this repo's actual dev-container Node version, and that the resulting test file is genuinely unchecked by the frontend's static-verify gate -- non-blocking (the PR's own functionality, tests, lint, and type-check all pass; this is a gap in defense-in-depth, not a correctness bug in the shipped change), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's rule that every non-blocking finding gets a tracked follow-up task.

checklist.step: The decisions entry on frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups claims (as one of two reasons the extracted rule module was kept as plain JS with JSDoc types rather than converted to real TypeScript): 'a sibling .ts file here would fail to load under plain Node ESM when eslint.config.js imports it directly (verified empirically: yarn lint with this file renamed to .ts throws a syntax error at the type-annotation tokens before any rule runs)'. Re-ran that exact experiment in this repo's actual dev container (node --version: v22.23.2, confirmed via `node --help` that `--no-experimental-strip-types` exists, i.e. type-stripping is ON by default in this Node version): renamed frontend/eslint-rules/no-restricted-src-import.js to .ts (content unchanged, updated eslint.config.js's import specifier to match) and ran `yarn lint` -- it passed cleanly, no syntax error. Went further and appended genuine (non-JSDoc) TypeScript syntax to the renamed file -- a typed function signature, an `interface`, a `type` alias, and a generic function -- and both `yarn lint` and a direct `node -e "import(...)"` probe loaded it without error. So the claimed empirical verification does not hold on this toolchain: Node's native type-stripping (on by default here) handles a plain-erasable-syntax .ts sibling file fine regardless of ESLint's own entry-file-only transpilation behavior, and this project's tsconfig.app.json/tsconfig.node.json already set `erasableSyntaxOnly: true` project-wide, i.e. exactly the syntax subset Node's stripping supports. The other stated reason (mirroring eslint.config.js's own pre-existing untyped/tsconfig-excluded status) still stands on its own and may well have been sufficient by itself -- but the decision entry's specific Node/ESM-loader empirical claim is factually wrong for this repo as it stands today and should be corrected (per CLAUDE.md's append-only correction convention: a fresh decisions entry noting the correction, not an in-place edit of the original text, since this doesn't meet the narrow in-place-edit carve-out).

Because frontend/eslint-rules/ sits outside both tsconfig.app.json's (`include: ["src", "tests", ".storybook"]`) and tsconfig.node.json's (`include: ["vite.config.ts", "playwright.config.ts"]`) project graphs, the new frontend/eslint-rules/no-restricted-src-import.test.ts -- a genuine TypeScript file with real type annotations (e.g. `Array<[label: string, source: string, blocked: boolean]>`, a type-cast in the wiring test) -- is never type-checked by `yarn tsc -b --noEmit`, and eslint's own config only applies `tseslint.configs.recommended` (not a type-aware `recommendedTypeChecked`) to it, so eslint doesn't catch type errors there either. Verified concretely: changed one test-table call from `isBlockedSrcSource(source)` to `isBlockedSrcSource(42)` (passing a `number` where the function's JSDoc/real signature expects a `string`) -- both `yarn lint` and `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` stayed clean (exit 0, no findings), and the bug was only caught by actually running `yarn vitest run eslint-rules` (which failed loudly with a runtime TypeError, since `isBlockedSrcSource` calls `.startsWith()` on the argument). In this specific case the runtime failure is immediate and loud, but the general risk -- a type error or wrong import in this test file going unnoticed by the repo's own static-verify gate, the exact 'trap' scenario this task's own review was asked to check for -- is real, not hypothetical, given Node's native stripping would in fact let a tsconfig-included version of this exact file (and the .js module, converted to .ts) type-check cleanly today. Worth deciding whether to add frontend/eslint-rules/ to tsconfig.app.json's include (or a small dedicated tsconfig project) now that the Node-loader objection to doing so doesn't hold, closing this gap for both the rule module and its test.

decisions.decision: Closed the type-checking gap by adding `eslint-rules` to `tsconfig.node.json`'s `include` array (alongside its existing `vite.config.ts`/`playwright.config.ts`) and turning on `allowJs` in that same project -- not `tsconfig.app.json`, not a new dedicated tsconfig project, and not `checkJs`. Proved the fix empirically, not just by editing config: with `allowJs` added but before fixing the test file's own type-unsoundness, `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` immediately surfaced three real pre-existing type errors in `no-restricted-src-import.test.ts` (an untyped `.find` callback parameter and two `TS7016 implicitly has an 'any' type` errors on the `.js` imports) -- fixed by removing the hand-written, incompatible-with-real-types `entry is {...}` type predicate on the `eslintConfig.find(...)` callback (its loosely-typed custom shape wasn't assignable to the real `TSESLint.FlatConfig.Config` type `tseslint.config(...)`'s declared return type gives the import once `allowJs` lets `tsc` see it) and instead casting the whole `eslintConfig` import once, at the top of the file, to the `eslint` package's own `Linter.Config[]` (`as unknown as Linter.Config[]`, documented inline) -- needed because `typescript-eslint`'s `FlatConfig.Config`/`Plugin`/`Processor` types and `eslint`'s own `@eslint/core`-derived `Linter.Config`/`Plugin` types are structurally incompatible in both directions (verified: `Partial<Record<string, Processor>>` vs `Record<string, Processor> | undefined` on the `processors` field alone fails assignability either way), even though both describe the same real flat-config object at runtime -- so a single explicit cast at the one place this file crosses from one package's types to the other's is more honest than fighting the mismatch property-by-property. Then re-proved the gap is closed the way the task asked: reinjected `isBlockedSrcSource(42)` (reverting the test-table call from `source` to a literal `42`) and confirmed `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` now fails with `TS2345: Argument of type 'number' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string'` (exit 2) -- it did not before this change -- then reverted it and reconfirmed a clean `tsc -b --noEmit`, a clean `yarn vitest run eslint-rules` (21/21), and a clean `yarn lint`. Also re-verified `yarn lint` still fires the rule on a real violation by adding a throwaway `tests/e2e/__probe_violation.spec.ts` importing a page component and confirming ESLint reports it, then deleting the probe file.
decisions.rationale: tsconfig.node.json over tsconfig.app.json: eslint-rules/ is build/tooling code (same category as vite.config.ts/playwright.config.ts, which already live in this project), not application code under src/tests/.storybook -- adding it to tsconfig.app.json would mean the app-code project's DOM/JSX-flavored compilerOptions (lib: ['ES2023','DOM'], jsx: 'react-jsx', types: ['vite/client','vitest/globals']) govern a Node-side tooling file for no reason, and would make a future app-code change to tsconfig.app.json's include semantics (e.g. a stricter per-directory rule) have to account for an unrelated tooling directory. allowJs without checkJs: allowJs is the minimum needed for tsc to resolve the .js import specifiers (no-restricted-src-import.test.ts importing from '../eslint.config.js' and './no-restricted-src-import.js') and infer their real exported types instead of falling back to 'any' -- this alone was enough to make every type annotation in the test file (the actual, concrete gap the task demonstrated with isBlockedSrcSource(42)) genuinely checked. Tried checkJs too (to also check the rule module's own internal code, per the task's 'ideally the rule module alongside it' framing) and it surfaced ~9 real errors (e.g. TS2339 'importKind'/'exportKind'/'specifiers' not existing on the generic estree AST node types the module's JSDoc currently annotates parameters with) that would need the module's JSDoc rewritten against TSESLint's own AST node types (not just estree's) to fix properly -- a nontrivial, higher-risk change to the one well-tested, five-times-regression-fixed predicate this whole task chain exists to protect, for a benefit (catching a type error in internal AST-handling code that's already exercised end-to-end by the wiring test's real Linter.verify() calls) much smaller than closing the test file's own gap. Left checkJs off and documented the narrower scope in docs/architecture/Testing.md rather than silently claiming more coverage than was actually added. Did not convert the module to real TypeScript (the option Item B's correction opened up): weighed it against churn -- the module works, is heavily commented, and converting would mean redoing exactly the same AST-node-typing work checkJs would have required (TSESTree node types for context/node parameters), for no additional type-checking benefit over the allowJs-only fix already made (allowJs resolves a plain .js module's JSDoc-inferred exported types for a .ts consumer just as well as a native .ts module would); kept it plain JS and recorded this as a considered-and-declined option rather than silently doing it.

decisions.decision: Per CLAUDE.md's Decision memory section, this is an append-only correction to frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups's existing decisions entry, not an in-place edit: that task's own checklist/review never asked for the decisions-text itself to be fixed (unlike backend-cftc-cot-data-followups's PR #274 case, where the checklist item literally called for a 'decisions-text update'), so the narrow in-place-edit carve-out doesn't apply here and the default (a fresh entry, leaving the original recoverable via git history) governs. This task's own checklist items above record the correction and its empirical re-verification; no edit was made to the other task's done file.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the append-only log property CLAUDE.md documents the carve-out as protecting: a reader of frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups's decisions entry today still sees exactly what was claimed and justified at the time (including the now-corrected Node/ESM-loader claim), and finds the correction, with its own timestamp and rationale, here instead -- rather than this task silently rewriting another already-done task's historical record.

comments.summary: Verified: the test file is now genuinely type-checked by tsc -b --noEmit (reproduced isBlockedSrcSource(42) both via the exact call-site change and via a tuple-literal type error; got TS2345/TS2322 respectively, where it previously passed silently). Verified the module itself (no-restricted-src-import.js) is NOT checked (checkJs off): injecting a real type error into it (calling .toFixed() on a string param) left tsc -b --noEmit at exit 0, only caught at runtime by yarn lint/vitest -- matches the task's own honest 'partial' framing, and docs/architecture/Testing.md states this accurately (does not overclaim).

Verified the eslint/typescript-eslint flat-config type incompatibility claim: Partial<Record<string, Processor>> (typescript-eslint's Config) is genuinely not assignable to Record<string, Processor> | undefined (eslint's own Linter.Config, from @eslint/core) via a plain assignment -- confirmed with an isolated tsc probe (TS2322, index-signature strictness). So a cast is genuinely required, as claimed.

Mutation-tested the wiring suite twice (severity flipped to 'off', and the rule's registration removed from the plugin object entirely) against the real eslint.config.js -- both mutations make the wiring describe block fail as expected, confirming the cast doesn't mask a genuine detection gap. allowJs side effects checked: no other stray .js files are newly pulled into tsconfig.node.json's project beyond eslint.config.js itself (pulled in transitively via the test's import, not type-checked since checkJs is off, no new errors); yarn build and a from-scratch yarn tsc -b --noEmit --force are both clean; removing allowJs reproduces the exact TS7016 implicit-any errors on both .js imports the PR's decisions entry describes, confirming allowJs is what makes them resolve as typed rather than any. checkJs-off claim spot-checked by temporarily enabling it: reproduces exactly ~9 errors (counted: 9), all TS2339/TS7006 on the rule module's generic-estree-typed AST node parameters (importKind/exportKind/specifiers missing, implicit-any context/node) -- matches the claim precisely, and I agree the scope call is reasonable: this chain's historical 5 rounds of regressions were all in the isBlockedSrcSource/BLOCKED_SRC_VALUE_IMPORT string-matching logic (now fully covered by the table test under real typing), not in the AST-node-handling code checkJs would additionally guard, and that code is already exercised behaviorally by the wiring tests' real Linter.verify() calls.

Non-blocking: a direct, single-hop `as Linter.Config[]` cast (no `unknown` detour) also compiles cleanly in place of the `as unknown as Linter.Config[]` used -- verified empirically (swapped the cast, ran a from-scratch tsc -b --noEmit --force, clean). The two types aren't mutually assignable, but TS's looser comparability check for a bare `as` assertion accepts them directly; going through `unknown` fully defeats that check instead of merely bridging the specific incompatible field, which is strictly less safe for no benefit here (confirmed: `number as unknown as Linter.Config[]` raises no error, while `number as Linter.Config[]` correctly fails with TS2352). Independently confirmed by a concurrently-run code-review pass. Filed as frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups.

Non-blocking (flagged by the concurrently-run code-review pass, reviewed and agreed): docs/architecture/Testing.md's claim that 'every real type annotation in the test file now is[checked]... against the real exported types of both modules' overstates the wiring-test block specifically -- post-cast, `eslintConfig` is checked against eslint's own `Linter.Config` (the cast target), not against eslint.config.js's actual declared `TSESLint.FlatConfig.Config[]` return type, since the cast at the import boundary substitutes one for the other. The isBlockedSrcSource-table block (no cast involved) is unaffected and is checked against the real type as claimed. Added to the same follow-up task.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran everything: backend pytest 1655 passed/99.95% coverage; frontend yarn lint and yarn tsc -b --noEmit both clean; yarn vitest run --coverage 105 files/1104 tests passed (99.78-99.84%); scripts/validate_tasks.py clean. Mutation-tested the wiring suite (flipped severity to 'off') and confirmed it fails as expected, so the cast isn't masking a detection gap.
